rules.title: A route is a `#[Route]` compiled into the unit's table, and its three runtime bugs are compile errors
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no runtime registry and no routes file — a `$router->get(...)` call has no counterpart, and a duplicate route, an unbound placeholder or a stale link name fails the build rather than a request

rules.title: `#[Route]` is `{path, method, name?}` on a method, recognized by name and never by shape
rules.divergesFromPhp: the attribute is read while compiling rather than by a reflection scan at boot, a route's name is never derived from the class and method, and there is no class-level prefix attribute

rules.title: A path is literal segments and three capture forms, each capture a whole segment naming a parameter
rules.divergesFromPhp: `{name}` rather than `:name`, a capture is always a whole segment so `/u{id}` and `/{id}.json` are refused rather than partially matched, and there is no inline constraint — the parameter's type is the constraint

rules.title: There is no wildcard verb: `method` is required, singular, and one case of a closed enum
rules.divergesFromPhp: `Route::any()` and `methods: ['*']` have no spelling — each verb a route answers is its own `#[Route]` line, because `Allow:` and the CSRF classification read the exact set

rules.title: Precedence is structural — a literal beats a capture beats an optional beats a catch-all — never declaration order
rules.divergesFromPhp: a routes file is not read top to bottom — first-match-wins does not exist, so moving a declaration between files cannot change which route answers

rules.title: A capture narrows to a closed set with a literal-union or enum-subset type, never with a regex
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `->where('lang', 'en|de|fr')`; the constraint is the parameter's type, and a regex on a route is refused outright

rules.title: An enum capture is spelled by a written backing value, and by its case name when the value was counted
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no backed-versus-pure split to route on — every enum is integer-backed, so what decides the spelling is whether the value was written

rules.title: `{name?}` captures one trailing segment or none, and its parameter's default is what makes the absent case well-typed
rules.divergesFromPhp: an optional segment is declared by the parameter's default, not by a second route or an optional regex group, and `/posts/` does not match `/posts/{page?}`

rules.title: A `#[Query]` parameter is declared with a capture's type list, and a default is what makes it optional
rules.divergesFromPhp: a query key is declared on the handler's parameter with a type, matched nominally as `Core\Query`, rather than read out of `$_GET` and validated by hand

rules.title: A query value that fails to convert is a `400`, where a path capture that fails is a `404`
rules.divergesFromPhp: a bad query value is refused with a 400 before the handler sees it, instead of arriving as a string the handler casts and checks

rules.title: One method's repeated routes may share a `name` only when they share a `path`; every other duplicate name is a compile error
rules.divergesFromPhp: a framework's `methods: ['POST', 'PUT']` on one named route becomes one `#[Route]` line per verb, each carrying the same `name` and the same `path`

rules.title: A shared name is one `url()` target, one `Match::name` for every verb, and one `operationId` per verb
rules.divergesFromPhp: the generated `operationId` is the route name, suffixed with the lowercased verb only where two operations share it — never a counter

rules.title: The router stops at matching: a match is a name and typed parameters, and nothing here dispatches
rules.divergesFromPhp: no framework router's dispatch is here — no controller base class, no middleware, no return-value-to-response rule, no `HEAD`-implies-`GET` or trailing-slash normalisation; the program or its framework writes the `switch`

rules.title: A match carries a name and typed parameters and nothing invocable, and typed `callable` would not change that
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `$route->getCallable()`; the handler is reached by a `switch` the framework generates or the application writes

rules.title: A request is matched once, before any application code runs, and `Core\Request::route()` is that match
rules.divergesFromPhp: the match is made by the server and read off the request, not by a framework kernel in userland that matches and then calls the controller

rules.title: The server's match dispatches nothing, and a request the table does not claim is served by the program
rules.divergesFromPhp: a matched route never calls anything; the program or the framework dispatches, and a `null` route is a fact the program reads rather than a 404 anything sends

rules.title: A missing path and a refused verb are different answers, and `methodsFor` is what tells them apart
rules.divergesFromPhp: a wrong verb on a known path is a 405 with an `Allow:` list asked of the table, rather than the 404 a hand-rolled dispatch falls into

rules.title: `Core\Request::mount()` answers the prefix the door stripped and the tainted host captures, and it is never `null`
rules.divergesFromPhp: the deployment prefix is never derived from `REQUEST_URI` or `SCRIPT_NAME`; the server hands it over, and a tenant is a mount capture rather than a `host` field on the route

rules.title: `Core\Router::url` is a launderer whose literal name and `$params` are checked against the compiled table
rules.divergesFromPhp: a link is built from the route's name and checked while compiling, never assembled by hand — a renamed route fails the build at every stale `url()` rather than in a sent email

rules.title: A link carries the mount prefix the request arrived under, so one table serves at any mount
rules.divergesFromPhp: a link is never the declared path concatenated by hand, because the path a route is declared against is the mount-stripped one and the prefix is known only where the request is

rules.title: A `url()` key that is not a capture becomes a percent-encoded query string, and one that is neither a capture nor a declared `#[Query]` parameter does not compile
rules.divergesFromPhp: the query string is built by the same member that builds the path, and `url(...) . '?page=' . $n` is the concatenation the launderer exists to prevent

rules.title: `urlAbsolute` prepends a configured origin and never one sniffed from a request header
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no base URL derived from `$_SERVER['HTTP_HOST']`; an absolute link comes from a configured origin or the call throws

rules.title: An origin is declared per mount with `[app] origin` as the fallback, a request cannot set it, and a mount that calls `urlAbsolute` without one is a boot error
rules.divergesFromPhp: a multi-tenant deployment configures one origin line with a capture in it rather than computing a base URL per request

rules.title: The table is built by the program enumeration, and a program with no `#[Route]` builds none and pays nothing
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no route cache to warm or to go stale — the scan is compile-time work keyed and invalidated with the compiled unit

rules.title: The API document is generated from the route table while compiling, so it cannot drift from the code
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no hand-written or annotation-scanned OpenAPI file to keep in sync — the document is a build output of the route table, and a program with no `#[Route]` produces none

rules.title: `nvs build --openapi` writes OpenAPI 3.1 as a build artifact, and two builds of one source are byte-identical
rules.divergesFromPhp: no `/openapi.json` endpoint the running server assembles — the document is written at build time and served as a file, and there is no 3.0 or Swagger 2 output

rules.title: `nvs api diff` classifies every change as breaking, additive or cosmetic, and exits non-zero on a breaking one
rules.divergesFromPhp: a broken client contract is a failed build rather than a reviewer's judgement, and there is no suppression to wave one through

rules.title: A `#[Route]` missing its `path` gets a quick fix that offers a derived one, and nothing derives a path on its own
rules.divergesFromPhp: no convention routing — a class rename never moves a URL, because the derived path is inserted as source text once and is ordinary text from then on
